record.original_question: Characterize the graphs that admit overlapping-disc (sphere-of-influence) representations in the plane, and in particular decide whether K_9 has such a representation.

evidence.quote: Problem 8.9 Characterize those graphs with overlapping disc representations. Does K9 have such a representation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An overlapping-disc (or sphere-of-influence) representation of a finite simple graph G = (V,E) in the Euclidean plane is an assignment to each vertex v ∈ V of a closed disc D_v ⊂ R^2 such that two vertices u and v are adjacent in G if and only if the interiors of D_u and D_v overlap (i.e. their interiors have non-empty intersection, equivalently the open discs intersect). 

(a) Give a combinatorial characterization of the graphs G that admit such an overlapping-disc representation in the plane.

(b) Determine whether the complete graph K_9 on nine vertices admits an overlapping-disc representation in the plane.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for characterizations of overlapping-disc (sphere-of-influence) representations and the specific question about K_9 returned general literature on sphere-of-influence graphs, disk graphs, and intersection representations but no source establishing either a complete characterization of graphs with overlapping-disc representations or a definitive answer for K_9. The status of the problem could not be confirmed from available sources.

status_evidence.snippet: General theory and applications of sphere-of-influence graphs; no characterization or K_9 result given.
status_evidence.claim: Background literature exists on sphere-of-influence graphs but does not resolve the characterization or the K_9 question.

status_evidence.title: On the size of a random sphere of influence graph
status_evidence.snippet: Studies random sphere-of-influence graphs; does not address the deterministic characterization problem.
status_evidence.claim: Random-model results do not address the deterministic characterization or K_9.
